# flint — Fleet GitOps YAML Linter & Language Server

flint is installed on this system. Use it for linting, migrating, generating
and editing Fleet GitOps YAML configurations.

## When to use flint

Trigger this skill when the user mentions:
- Fleet GitOps YAML validation, linting, or fixing; "will gitops accept this?"
- Migrating a Fleet repo to a new version (teams->fleets, queries->reports)
- Adding software, profiles, policies, queries from real files (.pkg, .mobileconfig, .sql)
- Setting up an editor (VS Code, Zed, Sublime, Neovim) or git hooks
- Deprecated Fleet keys, broken `path:` references, directory structure
- Fleet policies, reports, labels, controls, software, agent_options
- fleetlint.toml configuration

## How to use

1. Run `flint help-ai` for the command index and SOP routing
2. Match user intent to the right SOP (`flint help-ai --sop <name>`):
   lint, migrate, lsp, hooks, author, paths, history, software, add-field
3. Run `flint help-ai --command <name>` for specific command flags
4. Use `--format json` (check, list-rules) or `--json` (dry-run, history) for machine-readable output

## Key commands

```
flint check .                                 # lint the repo (exit 1 on errors)
flint check . --fix                           # auto-fix safe issues
flint check . --format json                   # structured output
flint dry-run .                               # would `fleetctl gitops` accept this? (exit 2 = blocked)
flint migrate <path> --target-version latest  # migration report (JSON)
flint gen software --from <file.pkg>          # stanza from a real installer
flint init                                    # create fleetlint.toml
flint list-rules --format json                # all available rules
flint help-json                               # full CLI schema as JSON
```

## Important patterns

- Commands use SPACES: `flint help-ai` (NOT `flint help.ai`)
- Dots are ONLY for `--command` lookups: `flint help-ai --command gen.software`
- `--fix` auto-applies safe fixes, `--unsafe-fixes` for risky ones
- `flint migrate` outputs a JSON report -- does NOT apply changes
- Suppress a finding on one line: `# flint: ignore [rule-id]`
- The LSP (`flint lsp`) powers all editor extensions
- `fleetlint.toml` (or legacy `.fleetlint.toml`) configures rules, thresholds, files, and Fleet connection

## What flint validates (always available, no network needed)

- Required keys per file type (default.yml, fleet YAML, unassigned)
- Deprecated keys with version-gated severity (warning -> error -> removed)
- osquery platform compatibility (290 tables, osquery 5.23.1, darwin/windows/linux/chrome)
- SQL syntax validation for queries
- Structural validation (unknown keys, typo detection with suggestions)
- Cross-file references: `path:` targets exist, labels referenced = defined, policy auto-install hashes listed under software
- Date formats, hash formats, file extensions
- Secret hygiene (no hardcoded tokens in webhook URLs)
